title: Competing Soft Modes and Tunable Multicriticality in a Generalized Two-Mode Quantum Rabi Model
authors: Xiufeng Cao, Ofri Adiv, Neil G. R. Broderick
abstract: Multicritical phenomena play a central role in quantum many-body systems, yet their microscopic origin in light--matter platforms remains largely unexplored. Here we investigate a generalized two-mode quantum Rabi model with independently tunable rotating- and counter-rotating-wave couplings. We demonstrate that anisotropy lifts the parent U(1)-symmetric superradiant manifold with a gapless Goldstone-like mode by phase locking the complex superradiant order parameter. This phase-locking mechanism provides the common microscopic origin of the coordinate- and momentum-like soft-mode instabilities, the emergence of symmetry-related two- and four-triple-point multicritical topologies, and the corresponding thermodynamic responses. Within a unified Bogoliubov framework, we further show how the dominant soft mode is redistributed between the two symmetry-related instability channels, thereby determining the multicritical phase structure. The resulting phase boundaries are determined by collective soft-mode softening and coincide exactly with the mean-field instability conditions. We further show that the multicritical topology is directly encoded in the full quantum ground-state energy and its response functions, establishing a unified connection between phase topology, competing collective excitations, and thermodynamic observables. Our results identify competing soft-mode channels as the microscopic origin of tunable multicriticality in strongly coupled light--matter systems.
summary: This theoretical study analyzes a generalized two-mode quantum Rabi model to map out its multicritical phase diagram. By employing a unified Bogoliubov-deGennes framework, the authors show that anisotropy lifts a continuous symmetry, generating distinct multicritical topologies. The key finding is that competing soft-mode instabilities, derived from collective excitations, microscopically determine the system's phase boundaries.
main_problem: The paper investigates the microscopic origin and geometric organization of multicritical structures in quantum many-body systems, linking competing soft modes to phase topology.
main_result: Anisotropy lifts the U(1)-symmetric superradiant manifold, providing a common origin for coordinate- and momentum-like soft-mode instabilities that determine the multicritical phase structure.
method: The analysis employs a unified Bogoliubov-deGennes (BdG) framework applied to an effective low-energy Hamiltonian derived via Schrieffer-Wolff transformations.
model_or_system: The system is a generalized two-mode quantum Rabi model involving two bosonic modes and a two-level system, characterized by independently tunable rotating- and counter-rotating-wave couplings.
key_observables: Collective excitation spectrum ($\Omega_{N,\pm}$), ground-state energy ($E_{	ext{GS}}$), and soft-mode conditions derived from the vanishing of the lower Bogoliubov branch.
important_parameters: Tunable coupling strengths ($g_{a,b}, \lambda_{a,b}$), detuning ($\Delta_z$), and the ratio of coupling strengths to detuning.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the large-frequency-ratio regime to apply the Schrieffer-Wolff transformation and assumes the physical phase is determined by the global minimum of the quantum-corrected ground-state energy.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the phase diagram evolution, showing the transition from a U(1)-symmetric Goldstone phase to distinct multicritical topologies (two- or four-triple-point) upon introducing anisotropy.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the Hamiltonian and then analyzes the normal phase using BdG theory to find soft-mode conditions. It then extends this to the two superradiant branches (SRr and SRi), unifying the analysis across all three phases to map the full multicritical phase diagram.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous quantum many-body approach to understanding how microscopic couplings (like anisotropy) dictate the macroscopic phase diagram topology in light-matter interactions, which is central to quantum optics and cavity QED.
